subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Cannibalization Effects
description: A quick, practical guide to Cannibalization Effects.

hook.text: A company launches a new cola. Sales soar—but the original cola drops 40%. Net gain: almost zero.

buildup.text: Cannibalization happens when a new product steals sales from an existing one in the same portfolio.

discovery.text: Forecasting new products must account for the expected cannibalization of current products.

twist.text: Ignoring cannibalization leads to overstocking old products and understocking new ones simultaneously.

climax.text: Portfolio-level forecasting—modeling all products together—captures cannibalization and halo effects.

punchline.text: New product demand isn't always new demand. It's often shifted.

quiz.question: What is demand cannibalization?
options: A new product stealing sales from existing ones
